cards.greeting: お世話になっております (osewa ni natte orimasu), then a seasonal line.
cards.formality: Keigo in external mail. Surname + さん for colleagues, 様 for customers.
dos: Acknowledge receipt before asking for anything.
Pre-align proposals informally (nemawashi) before the meeting.
Give exact deadlines: date, time and time zone.
donts: Use first names without an invitation.
Say a flat no or correct someone in a group.
Demand a decision in the room.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse or send a message to a Japanese colleague.
cards.caveat: Common business norms. Individuals, teams and multinational offices vary widely.

cards.greeting: Namaste, or 'Dear Mr Sharma' for a first contact. A short warm line comes first.
cards.formality: Titles + surname for seniors; 'Sir'/'Madam' where the office uses it; Ms by default.
dos: Give the reason before the request, and follow up gently.
Route proposals through the relationship owner.
Ask about family, festivals and cricket once trust exists.
donts: Contradict a senior in a group thread.
Treat a polite 'we will try' as a firm commitment.
Comment on someone's English.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for an Indian colleague.
cards.caveat: India is highly diverse; state, language and company culture dominate.

cards.greeting: Sehr geehrte Frau Müller for a first contact; Guten Tag once the relationship exists.
cards.formality: Sie until 'du' is explicitly offered. Keep academic titles in writing.
dos: State position, evidence and the proposed fix.
Document decisions with owner, date and next step.
Arrive early; start and end on the minute.
donts: Use hype, superlatives or motivational slogans.
Argue from rank instead of data.
Switch to a first name without an invitation.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a German colleague.
cards.caveat: Start-ups, agencies and international teams often differ from this baseline.

cards.greeting: Hi Sam, - first name, one warm sentence, then the ask.
cards.formality: Low. Plain language, contractions, titles only for senior external contacts.
dos: Put the ask in the first two sentences.
Name the decision owner and the deadline.
Pair a problem with a proposed next step.
donts: Use pointed reminders like 'per my last email'.
Wait for consensus when an owner can decide.
Comment on age, health or appearance.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a US colleague.
cards.caveat: US norms vary by region, industry and company size.

cards.greeting: Dear Ms Patel for a first contact, then Hi Priya once she signs off that way.
cards.formality: Understated and hedged, but polite. Avoid superlatives and corporate Americanisms.
dos: Hedge clearly: 'I'm not sure that quite works, because...'
Take contested points offline.
Send materials before the meeting.
donts: Say 'with all due respect'.
Correct someone in public, even as a joke.
Ask about salary, politics, class or health.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a UK colleague.
cards.caveat: Sector and region (London vs elsewhere) shift the tone.

cards.greeting: 您好 and title + surname: 王经理 or 王总.
cards.formality: Titles and 您 carry the relationship; face (mianzi) is the currency.
dos: Raise problems privately, framed as a question.
Secure leadership approval before broad circulation.
Give a face-saving route to a revised position.
donts: Say a flat no in a group.
Read a deferral as agreement.
Mention Taiwan, Tibet, Xinjiang or party politics.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a Chinese colleague.
cards.caveat: Generational and regional differences inside China are large.

cards.greeting: Olá, Ana, tudo bem? - warm, first-name, with a real question.
cards.formality: First names with peers; senhor/senhora and titles for seniors. Mirror the other side.
dos: Spend a line on the relationship before the ask.
Give feedback privately and warmly.
Confirm verbal agreements in writing.
donts: Send a cold, template-like demand.
Publicly criticise a colleague.
Ask about salary or politics.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a Brazilian colleague.
cards.caveat: São Paulo, Rio and the Nordeste differ noticeably.

cards.greeting: As-salaam alaikum, and greet the most senior person first.
cards.formality: Titles and family names (Mr Al Mansoori, Dr Haddad). Formal external register.
dos: Invest in the relationship before expecting a decision.
Praise publicly, correct privately.
Adjust scheduling around prayer times and Ramadan.
donts: Ask about a colleague's wife or daughters.
Offer alcohol or lunch during fasting hours.
Discuss religion or regional politics.
cards.unlock_hint: Analyse a draft for a Gulf colleague.
cards.caveat: Emirati, expatriate and free-zone offices differ substantially.
